detailed_description:
The target video is a motion-graphics film with an editorial, printed look, framed horizontally at 16:9, built from a photographic layer and a graphic layer, and the product is the hero of every shot. There is no location and no environment: the background of every shot is one flat colour field, and no two consecutive shots use the same field. The graphic layer is made of very large bold sans-serif English words, flat colour blocks, a thin print grid, brackets, halftone dot textures and colour bands; it is perfectly clean with no grain and no noise, it never emits light and never casts a shadow, and it never covers the shoes or their details. The photographic layer keeps the real materials of the shoes, and in the two shots with her it keeps real skin, real hair and real fabric, but every shadow is graphic — hard-edged and offset — rather than photographic. The typography is the main actor: short words in heavy type, tightly spaced, filling the full width of the frame, entering and leaving on the beat of the music. One single hard easing curve governs the whole video: everything leaves fast, stops hard, and occasionally springs back once. Each shot is a different scene: no two consecutive shots repeat the same background colour, the same camera distance or the same graphic device, and no graphic device is used twice. The young woman appears in only two shots, and the pale blue of the shoes' lining is the only colour in the video and appears once. Only one single line of text appears at any moment.
[Shot 1] The video opens on a flat white field. The word "STEP" in very large heavy black sans-serif type slides in fast from the right edge and stops hard, filling the full width of the frame, and the instant it stops a graphite colour band wipes across the whole frame from left to right and clears it. No product and no person are in the frame.
[Shot 2] At 00:01.600, the field is graphite. <Subject 2> slides in from below as a clean photographic cut-out and stops hard in the centre of the frame with a hard-edged offset shadow, while a thin white print grid fades in behind the shoes and two white graphic brackets close in around them. No person is in the frame and the camera holds a static shot.
[Shot 3] At 00:03.200, the field is light grey and the first of the two shots with a person begins. <Subject 1>, the young woman from <Picture 1> with an oval face, large dark brown eyes, fair skin, a small nose, soft coral lips, a slim build, long straight dark brown hair with wispy see-through bangs, and round silver-rimmed glasses, wearing a newly designed matte black loose top and black wide trousers with no jewellery and wearing <Subject 2>, walks in from the left edge of the frame and stops in the right third of it, with a hard-edged offset shadow under her feet. The shoes stay the brightest thing in the frame. She does not look into the lens and her lips stay completely closed. The camera holds a static shot.
[Shot 4] At 00:04.800, the field is white and the subject is the product alone again. The layout scales up into a close view of the toe of <Subject 2>: the perforated toe panel, the stitched panels and the white laces. A halftone dot texture appears in one corner of the frame, and the word "SPORT" in very large heavy black type sweeps in from the left edge and passes behind the shoes, so the shoes occlude part of it as it travels. No person is in the frame.
[Shot 5] At 00:06.400, the field is black and the shot cuts to a medium view of the full side profile of <Subject 2>: the thick white sole, the black accent block at the heel and the knot of the white laces. Three flat blocks — white, light grey and graphite — sweep in from the top, the left and the bottom of the frame one after another, lock together into one horizontal band and slide across the frame behind the shoes. No person is in the frame and the camera holds a static shot.
[Shot 6] At 00:08.000, the field is light grey and the frame is divided by a print grid into nine squares, four of which flash in sequence with a different photographic detail of <Subject 2>: the toe panel, the laces, the thick sole and the pull tab at the heel. The word "HIGH" in large heavy black type slides in above the grid and stops hard. No person is in the frame.
[Shot 7] At 00:09.600, the field is white and the second of the two shots with a person begins: a medium shot cropped at the waist, so that only the legs of <Subject 1> are in frame, wearing <Subject 2> and the black wide trousers. She lifts one foot and holds it up so the thick white sole faces the lens, with a hard-edged offset shadow under the standing foot, and her face is not in the frame. One pale blue band sweeps horizontally across the frame behind her raised foot — the only colour in the whole video — and thins away as it leaves. The camera holds a static shot.
[Shot 8] At 00:11.200, the field is black and the subject is the product alone again. <Subject 2> slides fast across the frame from left to right as a clean cut-out with real motion blur on the shoes, and then the layout breaks apart: every word, block and line in the frame flies outward, turns in the air and flies back, reassembling into a new, tighter composition around the shoes standing still in the centre. The word "MOVE" in very large heavy white type slides in from the right edge and stops hard beside the shoes, filling the width of the frame on one single line. No person is in the frame.
[Shot 9] At 00:12.600, the field becomes a mid-grey band that wipes across the frame and stops. On that band a single line of English in-frame copy appears as part of the composition, never in a lower subtitle position, set in SF Pro Display Semibold on one single line: at 00:13.200 the first half, "White, worn,", fades in in near-black dark grey; at 00:13.700 the second half, "and moving.", fades in in pure white, and the first half shifts gently about 12 pixels to the left within the same line to make room. The whole line "White, worn, and moving." stays on one single line, never wraps, never splits into two rows, and holds steady until the final frame while the layout settles. No other text appears anywhere in the video at any time.

overall_soundscape:
A designed, printed sound bed rather than a realistic location: the crisp slap of a page turning, a heavy stamp hit, the click of a typewriter key, a low whoosh whenever a block or a word travels, one clean tick as each square of the grid flashes, and the soft friction of fabric and rubber in the two shots where she moves. No voice, no dialogue and no singing are heard at any point.

non_diegetic_music:
A hard breakbeat and electro-funk bed at about 128 BPM with a tight kick, a clipped bass, short synth stabs and a dry snare, with every cut landing on the beat; it leaves one half-beat of empty space as the layout breaks apart in [Shot 8], and it ends on one single hard hit within 0.2 seconds under the final copy line.
